123	## Decisions
124	
125	### 1. Name and place of the option
126	
127	| Option | Trade-off |
128	| --- | --- |
129	| **`data.include_event: bool = True`** | Sits next to `inputs_fields`, which it changes. `include_` is the repo's word for "add this to the result" (`include_archived`). Needs no migration. Breaks the "booleans are `is_<adjective>`" rule, which the repo applies to state in `flags`. This is config, not state. |
130	| `data.attach_event` | Same place. "Attach" already means file attachments in chat (`ContentBlock` type `attachment`, `dtos.py:393`). One word would have two meanings. |
131	| `flags.is_event_included` | Follows the `flags` naming rule. But `flags` holds run state (`is_active`, `is_valid`, `is_test`), set by the user switch or by the system. This option is how the inputs are built. A reader looking for mapping config looks in `data`. |
132	| `data.event: {include: true}` | Room for more options later. No second option is planned, so the nesting adds a level for nothing. |
133	
134	Classification (design-interfaces): role is config of the mapping. Owner is the user. It
135	changes per subscription, when the user edits it. Not a credential, not routing.
136	
137	### 2. Default for new and old automations
138	
139	| Option | Trade-off |
140	| --- | --- |
141	| **`True` as the field default; absent means on** | Old rows have no key, so they read `True`. Old automations start to work. No backfill. |
142	| Default off, backfill on | Needs a data migration for the same result. |
143	| `Optional[bool] = None`, `None` means on | Three states for one switch. The frontend must treat `null` and `undefined` both as on. |
144	
145	### 3. Where the event goes in the agent's inputs
146	
147	| Option | Trade-off |
148	| --- | --- |
149	| **Append to the last user message** | The runner takes the tail user message as the turn (`services/runner/src/protocol.ts:1077-1086`), so the agent reads the instruction and the event together. A string content stays a string; a list content gets one more text part. |
150	| A second user message after the instruction | The instruction becomes history, not the current turn. Some harnesses treat it as prior context. |
151	| A system message | `system` messages go to `AGENTS.md` text (`dtos.py:1715-1730`), not to the turn. The event is turn data, not standing instruction. |
152	| A sibling input key (`inputs.event`) | The agent handler never reads it (`handler.py:479`). This is today's broken workaround. |
153	
154	The shape rules, applied to the resolved inputs:
155	
156	| Resolved inputs | Result |
157	| --- | --- |
158	| `messages` list, last message has `role: "user"` | Event text appended to that message. |
159	| `messages` list, last message is not a user message | A new user message with the event text is appended. |
160	| `{}` (no mapping keys) | `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<event text>"}]}`. |
161	| Anything else (a completion mapping such as `{"number": 42}`, or the whole-context `"$"` mapping) | Unchanged. The `"$"` mapping already carries the event. A completion mapping names its own inputs. |
162	
163	The event text is built from two values of the event context block: `event_type` for the
164	header and `attributes` for the JSON. It does not hold the other keys of the block.
165	
166	Event text (agent-facing, shown in the run transcript):
167	
168	~~~text
169	
170	Event data (GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_EVENT):
171	```json
172	{
173	  "action": "opened",
174	  "number": 42,
175	  "title": "Fix the login page"
176	}
177	```
178	~~~
179	
180	- It starts with a blank line, because the runner joins text blocks with no separator.
181	- The JSON is `json.dumps(attributes, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)`.
182	- When `event_type` is absent, the header is `Event data:`.
183	- In the `{}` case the leading blank line is dropped.
184	
185	### 4. Size of the event text
186	
187	| Option | Trade-off |
188	| --- | --- |
189	| **No cap in this change** | Less code on both sides: the Python and TypeScript formats stay one header and one JSON block. The whole-context `"$"` mapping already sends the full payload with no cap today. No recorded payload shows a size problem yet. |
190	| Cut the JSON at a fixed number of characters | Protects the model context from one very large payload. Adds a rule, a note line and a test on both sides, and the cut JSON is not valid JSON. |
191	| Drop large fields | Needs rules per field. More code for a case not seen yet. |
192	
193	QA records one real payload and its size (task 12.1). A cap is added in a later change if a
194	real payload is too large.
195	
196	### 5. Text coercion after resolution
197	
198	The resolver replaces a whole leaf with its value, so a pill on a number gives `text: 42`, on
199	an object gives a dict, and on an absent key gives `None`. Pydantic rejects the number and the
200	dict in the agent handler, so the run fails. `None` passes and sends an empty part (verified
201	with a script; see the research file). A pull request number is a common field, so this is
202	needed now.
203	
204	| Option | Trade-off |
205	| --- | --- |
206	| **The dispatcher coerces each message `content` and each text part `text` to a string** | One place, before the request is built and before the delivery is written. |
207	| Coerce in the SDK handler | Fixes it for every caller, but the runner and services can run a different SDK version than the API. The API fix works at once. |
208	| Make the frontend refuse pills on non-string fields | The schema can be wrong, and absent keys still give `None`. |
209	
210	The text rule, used by the dispatcher and by the frontend preview, so both give the same text:
211	
212	| Resolved value | Text |
213	| --- | --- |
214	| A string | The string, unchanged. |
215	| `None` (absent or null) | `""` |
216	| Anything else (number, boolean, object, list) | Compact JSON: `json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)` in Python, `JSON.stringify(value)` in TypeScript. `42` gives `42`, `true` gives `true`. |
217	
218	Coercion runs for subscriptions only, whether `include_event` is on or off. It touches only the
219	`messages` list. Schedules keep today's inputs: their messages are static text, and schedules
220	are out of scope.
221	
222	### 6. Recording the event on the delivery
223	
224	The preview needs real values. A delivery stores only resolved inputs.
225	
226	| Option | Trade-off |
227	| --- | --- |
228	| **`TriggerDeliveryData.event: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` = the context's `event` block** | The selector `$.event.attributes.title` resolves against `{event: delivery.data.event}` with no change. No migration. Stores the payload once more per delivery. |
229	| Show the newest delivery's `data.inputs` as it is | Needs no new field. But the preview cannot follow an edit of the instruction, and when the option is off the inputs hold only the pill values, not the other fields. |
230	| Parse the event JSON back out of the included text | Breaks when the option is off. Couples the screen to a text format. |
231	| No real values in the preview | The user cannot see a schema mismatch until the agent fails. |
232	
233	`data.event` holds the normalized event context block (`event_id`, `event_type`, `timestamp`,
234	`created_at`, `attributes`), not the raw provider body. The provider's `payload` is under
235	`attributes`.
236	
237	Set on subscription deliveries only (real runs, refusals that have the event, and test
238	captures). Schedules have a synthetic event; they keep `event` absent.
239	
240	### 7. Where the field cards come from
241	
242	| Option | Trade-off |
243	| --- | --- |
244	| **The catalog payload schema** | Available before the first event. Carries the provider's `description`. The query exists. |
245	| Keys of the newest delivery | Real keys, but empty until the first event, and no descriptions. |
246	| Both, merged | Handles a schema mismatch, but adds merge rules before we know a mismatch happens. |
247	
248	Card rules:
249	
250	- One card per property of `payload.properties`, in schema order.
251	- A property of type `object` with its own `properties` is a group: the group shows its
252	  humanized name and one card per child property. Deeper objects are one card each.
253	- An array is one card.
254	- Label: split camelCase into words, then `humanizeActionKey` from `@agenta/shared/utils`
255	  (`web/packages/agenta-shared/src/utils/toolSlug.ts:67-81`). `createdBy` reads "Created by",
256	  `htmlUrl` reads "Html URL". A child label is the parent and child words together:
257	  `data.title` reads "Data title". No hand-written label map.
258	- Description: the property's `description`, as the provider wrote it. No description: no line.
259	- Selector: `$.event.attributes.<key>`, or `$.event.attributes["<key>"]` when the key is not
260	  letters, digits and underscores.
261	- A card shows a check when the template already has its selector.
262	- No schema, or an empty `properties`: no cards. The checkbox and the preview still show.

265	
266	Run now opens a new chat with the instruction. It has no event of its own.
267	
268	| Option | Trade-off |
269	| --- | --- |
270	| **Send the preview text. The preview fills pills from the newest delivery's event and adds the event text when the option is on. With no delivery, each pill becomes its label in square brackets.** | One function builds the text for the preview and for Run now, so Run now sends what the preview shows. The user tests with real data when it exists. Today Run now sends the joined text, which would hold raw selectors once pills exist, so a change is needed now. |
271	| Send pills as raw selectors | The agent reads `$.event.attributes.title`. Wrong. |
272	| Block Run now until a delivery exists | A new automation cannot be tried at all. |

274	The frontend builds the text with the same rules as the dispatcher:
275	
276	- Pill values follow the text rule of decision 5.
277	- The header reads `event_type` from the delivery's `data.event`, the same value the dispatcher
278	  uses, not the automation's event key.
279	- The frontend lookup keeps a quoted key whole: `$.event.attributes["a.b"]` reads the key
280	  `a.b`. Today `resolveSelectorPreview` splits it into `a` and `b`
281	  (`web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/core/selectorPreview.ts:34-38`); this
282	  change fixes that.

284	Two limits on Run now:
285	
286	- **A mapping the composer cannot show** (several messages, a non-user message, a non-text
287	  part; see decision 10) is not built by the new function. The preview shows only today's
288	  warning line, and Run now sends today's text (`getScheduleMessagePreview` of the stored
289	  inputs). This keeps today's behavior for agent-made mappings and avoids a second general
290	  message builder in the frontend. `parseMessageTemplate` must tell this case apart from an
291	  empty instruction.
292	- **The newest event is read when the user presses Run now**, with one awaited call to
293	  `queryTriggerDeliveries`. A pure function, `latestDeliveryEvent(deliveries)`, picks the
294	  newest delivery that has `data.event`. The preview calls the same function on the rows of
295	  `useAutomationRuns`, so the rule lives in one place. Both entry points (the detail button and the
296	  list menu) do this, so neither starts a run while the deliveries are still loading, and the
297	  list does not run one deliveries query per row. Labels in square brackets are used only when

302	This is a contract for the selectors the cards make, not a general JSON Path engine. Both
303	sides have tests with the same fixtures: the event text example of decision 3, a string, a

322	### 10. Reading and writing the mapping
323	
324	`parseMessageTemplate` returns `""` when the mapping has any key other than the message
325	(`eventMessageTemplate.ts:126-138`). A builder agent's mapping often has a sibling `event` key,
326	so the screen would show an empty box and Save would drop that key.
327	
328	Decision: `parseMessageTemplate` reads the message and ignores other keys. It returns
329	`string | null`: `null` means the composer cannot show the mapping, the same meaning
330	`contentToTemplate` gives `null` (`eventMessageTemplate.ts:84`). `compileMessageTemplate` has
331	no caller today, so it changes in place instead of getting a second writer next to it: it takes
332	the stored `inputsText`, replaces only the message key and keeps the rest, the same rule
333	`setScheduleMessage` follows (`messageInputs.ts:100-118`). One function writes a template into
334	a mapping. A mapping the composer cannot show (several messages, a non-user message, a non-text
335	part) keeps today's warning line and is replaced only when the user types.
336	
337	The Instruction field also moves the message when the agent's input shape resolves late
338	(`remapMessageShape`, `messageInputs.ts:132-143`, called from
339	`AutomationInstructionField.tsx:62-77`). That helper reads plain text only, so a text with a
340	pill typed before a chat agent resolves would stay under the old key, where the agent does not
341	read it. For event automations, a new `remapMessageTemplate(inputsText, prev, next)` does the
342	same move with `parseMessageTemplate` and `compileMessageTemplate`: it removes the old key,
343	keeps sibling keys, and leaves a mapping it cannot show untouched. Schedules keep
344	`remapMessageShape`.

347	
348	| Option | Trade-off |
349	| --- | --- |
350	| **Fix `_TRIGGER_INPUTS_REFERENCE` in this change** | A text edit. Today the text tells builder agents to add a sibling `event` key that the agent handler never reads, so every agent-made automation gets a mapping that does not work. The fix stops new broken mappings now. |
351	| Fix it in a later change | Builder agents keep making the broken mapping until then. With `include_event` on, those runs still get the event, but the mapping carries a dead key. |

353	## Risks / Trade-offs
354	
355	- **The delivered keys may not match the schema.** Not verified: no real delivery is on record
356	  in the repo or the local databases. If a key differs, its pill gives an empty string, and the
357	  included event still carries the real key. QA records one real GitHub payload and compares.
358	- **Old automations change behavior.** Their agents start to get the event text. That is the
359	  fix, but a prompt that depended on not seeing it may act differently. The user can turn the
360	  option off.
361	- **The transcript shows the event JSON.** The included text is part of the user message, so the
362	  session view shows it. This is honest about what the agent got.
363	- **Storage.** Each subscription delivery stores the payload in `data.event`, and, when the
364	  option is on, a second copy inside `data.inputs`. Composio payloads are small JSON objects.
365	  No cap on the stored copy.
366	- **Typed text that starts with `$` or `/`** is read as a selector by the resolver, today and
367	  after this change (`resolvers.py:128-133`). Recorded as a known limit.
368	- **Two copies of the text rules** (Python and TypeScript): the event text format and the pill
369	  value rule. Pinned by the same fixtures in both test suites (decision 8).
370	- **A very large payload** goes to the agent in full, with no cap (decision 4).
371	- **Version skew.** The SDK reference text ships with the SDK. The dispatcher change ships with
372	  the API. Neither depends on the other.
373	
374	## Migration
375

382	## ADDED Requirements
383	
384	### Requirement: Field cards for event automations
385	
386	For an event automation, the Instruction field SHALL show a grid of field cards under the instruction box, built from the catalog payload schema of the automation's event. Schedules SHALL keep today's composer.
387	
388	#### Scenario: Flat schema
389	
390	- **WHEN** the event is the GitHub pull request event, whose schema has `action`, `createdAt`, `createdBy`, `description`, `number`, `title` and `url`
391	- **THEN** seven cards show, in schema order, each with its humanized name and the schema's `description`
392	
393	#### Scenario: Nested object
394	
395	- **WHEN** a property is an object with its own `properties`, such as Linear's `data`
396	- **THEN** the object shows as a group named for it, with one card per child property, and deeper objects show as one card each
397	
398	#### Scenario: No schema
399	
400	- **WHEN** the catalog returns no payload schema, or the query fails
401	- **THEN** no cards show and the instruction box, the checkbox and the preview still work
402	
403	### Requirement: Card labels come from the key
404	
405	A card label SHALL be the property key split at camelCase and underscores, in sentence case, with known acronyms in capitals, through `humanizeActionKey`. A child label SHALL join the parent and child words. No hand-written label map SHALL exist.
406	
407	#### Scenario: camelCase key
408	
409	- **WHEN** the key is `createdBy`
410	- **THEN** the label is "Created by"
411	
412	#### Scenario: Acronym
413	
414	- **WHEN** the key is `url`
415	- **THEN** the label is "URL"
416	
417	### Requirement: Pills
418	
419	A click on a card SHALL insert a pill for that field at the cursor. The pill SHALL show the card label. The mapping SHALL store the field as the selector `$.event.attributes.<key>`. A pill SHALL be removable like one character.
420	
421	#### Scenario: Insert
422	
423	- **WHEN** the user types "Review " and clicks the "Title" card
424	- **THEN** the box shows "Review " and a "Title" pill, and the stored content is `[{"type":"text","text":"Review "},{"type":"text","text":"$.event.attributes.title"}]`
425	
426	#### Scenario: Used card
427	
428	- **WHEN** the instruction already has a "Title" pill
429	- **THEN** the "Title" card shows a check
430	
431	#### Scenario: Remove
432	
433	- **WHEN** the user deletes the pill with Backspace
434	- **THEN** the selector leaves the stored content and the card loses its check
435	
436	#### Scenario: Key with special characters
437	
438	- **WHEN** a key has a character other than letters, digits and underscores
439	- **THEN** the selector uses bracket form, `$.event.attributes["<key>"]`
440	
441	### Requirement: Other mapping keys are kept
442	
443	Reading and writing the instruction SHALL change only the message key of the mapping and SHALL keep every other key.
444	
445	#### Scenario: Agent-made mapping
446	
447	- **WHEN** a stored mapping is `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Triage it"}],"event":"$.event.attributes"}` and the user edits the text
448	- **THEN** the saved mapping still has the `event` key
449	
450	#### Scenario: Pill typed before the agent's input shape resolves
451	
452	- **WHEN** the user types text and inserts a pill before the agent revision resolves, and the agent then resolves as a chat agent
453	- **THEN** the text and the pill move into `messages`, the old key is removed, and other keys are kept
454	
455	### Requirement: Include-event checkbox
456	
457	The Instruction field SHALL show a checkbox labeled "Also attach the full event, so the agent can use any detail" for event automations. It SHALL read `data.include_event`, treat an absent value as checked, and save its value with the rest of the draft.
458	
459	#### Scenario: Existing automation
460	
461	- **WHEN** an automation saved before this change opens
462	- **THEN** the checkbox is checked
463	
464	#### Scenario: New automation
465	
466	- **WHEN** the user creates an event automation and does not touch the checkbox
467	- **THEN** the create payload has `data.include_event` equal to `true`
468	
469	#### Scenario: Unsaved change
470	
471	- **WHEN** the user unchecks it on the detail screen
472	- **THEN** the save bar shows, and Discard checks it again
473	
474	### Requirement: What the agent gets preview
475	
476	The Instruction field SHALL show a "What the agent gets" preview of the message. Pills SHALL show values from `data.event` of the newest delivery that has one, with the same text rule as the dispatcher (a string unchanged, an absent or null value empty, any other value as compact JSON), else their labels. When the checkbox is on, the preview SHALL show that the full event is added, with its JSON when a delivery has one.
477	
478	#### Scenario: With a delivery
479	
480	- **WHEN** the newest delivery with `data.event` has `attributes.title` equal to "Fix the login page"
481	- **THEN** the "Title" pill reads "Fix the login page" in the preview
482	
483	#### Scenario: Without a delivery
484	
485	- **WHEN** no delivery has `data.event`
486	- **THEN** the pills show their labels and the preview states that the full event is added when one arrives
487	
488	#### Scenario: Quoted key
489	
490	- **WHEN** a pill's selector is `$.event.attributes["a.b"]` and the delivery's attributes have the key `a.b`
491	- **THEN** the preview shows the value of `a.b`
492	
493	### Requirement: Run now uses the same message
494	
495	Run now SHALL send the text the preview shows, built by the same function: pills filled from the newest delivery with `data.event`, each pill as its label in square brackets when there is none, and the event text added when the checkbox is saved as on and an event exists.
496	
497	#### Scenario: Run now with a delivery
498	
499	- **WHEN** the user presses Run now and a delivery with `data.event` exists
500	- **THEN** the new chat's first message has the filled values and, when the option is on, the event text in the dispatcher's format
501	
502	#### Scenario: Run now with pills and no delivery
503	
504	- **WHEN** the deliveries call succeeds and no delivery has `data.event`
505	- **THEN** the first message has "[Title]" where the "Title" pill is
506	
507	#### Scenario: Deliveries call fails
508	
509	- **WHEN** the user presses Run now and the deliveries call fails
510	- **THEN** no run starts, the error goes to the log, and the button stays enabled
511	
512	#### Scenario: Mapping the composer cannot show
513	
514	- **WHEN** the stored mapping has several messages, a non-user message or a non-text part
515	- **THEN** the preview shows only the existing warning line and Run now sends the same text it sends today
516	## ADDED Requirements
517	
518	### Requirement: Include-event option on subscriptions
519	
520	A trigger subscription SHALL carry `data.include_event`, a boolean that defaults to true. A stored subscription without the key SHALL read as true.
521	
522	#### Scenario: Old subscription reads as on
523	
524	- **WHEN** a subscription row was saved before this change and its `data` has no `include_event` key
525	- **THEN** the API returns it with `data.include_event` equal to `true`
526	
527	#### Scenario: The user turns it off
528	
529	- **WHEN** a client edits a subscription with `data.include_event` set to `false`
530	- **THEN** the stored row keeps `false` and later reads return `false`
531	
532	#### Scenario: No migration
533	
534	- **WHEN** the change is deployed
535	- **THEN** no database migration runs, because `data` is a JSON column
536	
537	### Requirement: Event included in the agent's message
538	
539	When `include_event` is true and the event has attributes, the dispatcher SHALL add the event text to the resolved inputs of a subscription before it sends them. The event text is a blank line, a header that names `event.event_type`, and the JSON of `event.attributes` in a fenced block, with no size cap.
540	
541	#### Scenario: Chat mapping with a string instruction
542	
543	- **WHEN** the resolved inputs are `{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Review this pull request"}]}`
544	- **THEN** the sent content is `"Review this pull request"` followed by the event text, as one string
545	
546	#### Scenario: Chat mapping with text parts
547	
548	- **WHEN** the last user message has a list of text parts
549	- **THEN** one more text part with the event text is appended to that list
550	
551	#### Scenario: Last message is not a user message
552	
553	- **WHEN** the resolved `messages` list ends with a message whose role is not `user`
554	- **THEN** a new user message with the event text is appended
555	
556	#### Scenario: Empty mapping
557	
558	- **WHEN** the mapping is `{}`
559	- **THEN** the inputs become one user message whose content is the event text without the leading blank line
560	
561	#### Scenario: Other mapping shapes stay unchanged
562	
563	- **WHEN** the resolved inputs have no `messages` list and are not empty, for example `{"number": 42}` or the whole context from a `"$"` mapping
564	- **THEN** the inputs are sent unchanged
565	
566	#### Scenario: Option off
567	
568	- **WHEN** `include_event` is false
569	- **THEN** no event text is added
570	
571	#### Scenario: Event without attributes
572	
573	- **WHEN** the event's `attributes` is absent or null
574	- **THEN** no event text is added
575	
576	### Requirement: Message text is always a string
577	
578	After it resolves the mapping of a subscription, the dispatcher SHALL turn each `content` value of a message in `messages`, and each `text` value of a text part in such a content list, into a string, whether or not `include_event` is on. A string SHALL stay unchanged, `None` SHALL become the empty string, and any other value SHALL become its compact JSON. Schedule inputs SHALL stay as they are today.
579	
580	#### Scenario: Number field
581	
582	- **WHEN** a text part's selector resolves to the integer `42`
583	- **THEN** the sent part is `{"type":"text","text":"42"}`
584	
585	#### Scenario: Object field
586	
587	- **WHEN** a selector resolves to an object
588	- **THEN** the sent text is the compact JSON of that object
589	
590	#### Scenario: Absent field
591	
592	- **WHEN** a selector resolves to nothing
593	- **THEN** the sent text is the empty string and the run does not fail
594	
595	#### Scenario: Boolean field
596	
597	- **WHEN** a selector resolves to `true`
598	- **THEN** the sent text is `true`, the same text the frontend preview shows
599	
600	### Requirement: Delivery records the event
601	
602	Each subscription delivery that the dispatcher writes with a resolved event SHALL store the normalized event context block (`event_id`, `event_type`, `timestamp`, `created_at`, `attributes`) in `data.event`, not the raw provider body. Schedule deliveries SHALL NOT set it.
603	
604	#### Scenario: Successful run
605	
606	- **WHEN** an event runs the agent
607	- **THEN** the delivery's `data.event.attributes` equals the provider payload and `data.inputs` equals the inputs sent, event text included
608	
609	#### Scenario: Schedule tick
610	
611	- **WHEN** a schedule fires
612	- **THEN** its delivery has no `data.event`
613	
614	### Requirement: Test captures match real runs
615	
616	A test-mode capture SHALL build its inputs with the same coercion and event text as a real run, and SHALL record `data.event`.
617	
618	#### Scenario: Test capture with the option on
619	
620	- **WHEN** a subscription with `flags.is_test` true and `include_event` true receives an event
621	- **THEN** the test delivery's `data.inputs` holds the event text and `data.event` holds the event
622	
623	### Requirement: Builder agent guidance
624	
625	The agent-facing reference on trigger inputs SHALL state that the event is included in the message by default and SHALL NOT recommend a sibling `event` input key.
626	
627	#### Scenario: Reference text
628	
629	- **WHEN** a builder agent reads the trigger inputs reference
630	- **THEN** it reads that `include_event` defaults to on and that the agent reads only `messages`

The loop stopped because three rounds ran, not because every lens rated Low. The owner fixed every finding of round 3 in the spec, but no reviewer has checked those fixes yet. Each later round found a new, smaller problem that the earlier fix exposed, and none of them questioned the scope of the change.

## The six parts the owner asked about

1. The new `data.event` field on each subscription delivery is kept. The preview must follow edits to the instruction and must show fields when the option is off, and the stored `data.inputs` cannot do either.
2. Run now filling pills from the newest delivery is kept. Today Run now sends the joined text, which would hold raw selectors such as `$.event.attributes.title` once pills exist. Run now now sends the same text as the preview, built by one function.
3. The text coercion of pill values that are not strings is kept, for subscriptions only. A number field, such as a pull request number, fails the run today. Schedules keep today's inputs, because their messages are static text.
4. The 20,000 character cap is cut. It added a rule, a note line and tests on both the Python and TypeScript sides. The `"$"` mapping already sends the full payload with no cap today, and no recorded payload shows a size problem. QA records the size of one real payload (task 12.1), and a cap comes in a later change if a payload is too large.
5. The restored `PillEditor.tsx` and the two new components are kept. `MessageComposer` is a plain text area and cannot hold a pill as one unit, so an event mode inside it would change the schedule editor. Restoring the old editor is less new code than writing one.
6. The fix to the builder agent reference text in `agenta_builtins.py` is kept in this change. It is a text edit, and the current text tells builder agents to add an `event` key that the agent never reads.

# API conventions (OSS + EE)

Scope: everything under `api/`. This file loads when you work in the API. The repo-wide
root conventions live in `/AGENTS.md`.

## Environment config conventions

- For API configuration, add new environment variables to `api/oss/src/utils/env.py` and
  consume them via the shared `env` object.
- Avoid calling `os.getenv(...)` directly in feature code when the value is part of
  application config.
- Avoid local imports inside helper functions for configuration lookup; prefer
  module-level imports unless there is a proven circular dependency.

## Formatting

Run `ruff format` then `ruff check --fix` within the API folder (from the repo root:
`ruff format` then `ruff check`). Fix all errors before committing.

## Code comments

Keep AI-generated in-code comments minimal. Comment only the non-obvious *why* (a subtle invariant, a workaround, a pool/concurrency hazard), never the *what* the code already states. Prefer one terse line over a multi-line block; do not narrate steps, restate the code, or leave TODO-style prose. If a comment is needed to explain *what* a block does, rename or extract instead.

## API Architecture Patterns

Use this section for all new work.

### API repo map

- `api/oss/src/*` is the OSS baseline API (new + legacy coexist here).
- `api/ee/src/*` is the EE extension API (billing, organizations, workspace, meters,
  subscriptions, throttling).
- `api/entrypoints/*` is the composition root (dependency wiring and route mounting).

OSS and EE relationship:
- OSS app is assembled first in `api/entrypoints/routers.py`.
- When `is_ee()` is true, EE extends that app via:
  - `ee.extend_main(app)` for extra routers/features.
  - `ee.extend_app_schema(app)` for OpenAPI/security metadata.
- EE is additive over OSS, not a separate API architecture.

RBAC / access enforcement:

- RBAC enforcement is an OSS feature and is always-on in both editions. The
  permission vocabulary, default role catalog, and enforcement service live in
  `api/oss/src/core/access/`. Handlers call `check_action_access(...)`
  unconditionally; it decides for the request's principal (the `RequestAccess` the auth
  middleware sets), and there is no edition gate around the check itself.
- The only edition difference is the EE plan gate: in EE, `check_entitlements(Flag.RBAC)`
  can grant allow-all to members when a plan is not RBAC-entitled. It enters through
  `RbacEnforcementInterface` (`oss/src/core/access/interfaces.py`); `entrypoints/access.py`
  wires `EntitlementsRbacEnforcement` (EE) or `AlwaysEnforcedRbac` (OSS). OSS never imports
  `ee.*` at module top.
- Custom roles are an EE feature: `AGENTA_ACCESS_ROLES` / `AGENTA_ACCESS_ROLES_OVERLAY`
  are parsed/applied in `api/ee/src/core/access/permissions/role_overrides.py` and
  ignored in OSS (which enforces the code-default catalog).

Project membership and access:

- Membership is decided only by `MembershipsService.resolve` (`oss/src/core/memberships/`) and its uncached form `read_membership` (same policy and DAO read; use it only where another cache keeps the outcome, today the Bearer workspace-only and no-parameter branches). No other membership reader or policy.
  OSS: every organization member is a member of every project, with the organization role.
  EE: a member needs an organization row and a `project_members` row; the project row's
  role applies. The edition policy is picked only in `entrypoints/access.py`.
- Membership writes go only through the four `MembershipsService` writers:
  `set_member_role`, `remove_member`, `create_project` (seeds every organization member in
  the same transaction) and `transfer_ownership`. Each writer clears the access caches with
  `invalidate_access_caches` after the commit. An admin tool that writes membership rows
  directly must call `invalidate_access_caches` too.
- `check_action_access` delegates to `AccessService.check_request`. Every process that
  checks access calls `bootstrap_access()` at startup (the API and both workers do).
- No new code reads `workspace_members` or `project_members` to decide access.
- No code creates or updates `workspaces` or `workspace_members` rows or writes
  `projects.workspace_id` (workspace removal step 2). The API answers the organization id
  where a workspace id was. Legacy workspace ids still map to their organization through
  `db_manager` (`_WORKSPACE_REF_CTE`, `get_workspace`) until step 2b removes those reads.
- A hot-path membership read is one SQL statement (`fetch_membership_row`,
  `list_membership_rows`). `integration/memberships/test_hot_path_query_counts_postgres.py`
  pins the counts.
- Revocation takes effect at the next decision. It can take up to `AGENTA_CACHE_TTL`
  (300 s) in two known cases: the Redis invalidation fails, or a read that started before
  the mutation committed refills the old entry after the invalidation.

Access layer invariants (run principal):

- Every run has an explicit `RunEnvelope` (principal, authority, run context, sender,
  approver). Routers get it from `request_run_envelope(request)`; durable work builds it
  with `stored_work_envelope`, `child_envelope` or `resumed_envelope`. No code builds a
  human principal from a bare user id.
- There is no implicit human fallback. `check_action_access` needs request access and
  raises without it (`RequestAccessMissing`) or for another user
  (`RequestAccessMismatch`). Code that checks another human, or runs without request
  access (callbacks exempt from the auth middleware, workers), calls
  `AccessService.check_human` or `decide` explicitly.
- `AccessService.decide` runs on every call. Nothing caches a decision. Only the
  principal record (`fetch_principal`), the membership (`resolve_membership`) and the
  project's organization are cached, and their writers invalidate them.
- Cached access DTOs give every `Optional` field a `None` default: the cache drops
  `None` fields when it serializes.
- Durable work (queued inputs, continuations, interactions, schedules, subscriptions,
  evaluation runs, channel turns, child runs) stores its envelope or principal and
  rechecks it with `require` (or `decide`) before it runs. A refusal is a terminal
  settlement (failed delivery and paused trigger, failed evaluation run, obsolete
  command, cancelled interaction), never a retry.
- Mint a run credential (`sign_secret_token`) only after the decision allows. The minted
  envelope copies the caller's; it never upgrades a principal.
- New agent-visible failures use `AgentError` (`access_denied`, `missing_principal`,
  `missing_envelope`).
- Access logs carry ids and kinds only, never a token, a header, raw claims or an
  envelope.
- `integration/access/test_run_principal_query_counts_postgres.py` pins the hot paths at
  zero access-decision statements on warm caches.

Access layer invariants (agent and session sharing):

- Every agent or session access calls `AccessService.decide` with a `ResourceRef`, and
  lists pass a read scope in SQL. List queries take a required read scope; there is no
  unrestricted scope.
- Every point where a run starts or resumes calls `RunAdmission` (`admit`, `admit_turn` or
  `admit_request`) with the stored or request envelope.
- `AccessService` requires a resource policy; every composition root passes
  `SharingService`.
- Never treat a null owner as "not migrated".
- Audit events carry identifiers, never credential values.

Organization-scoped decisions and organization credentials (M5):
- An organization subscription login (`subscription_provider` in `ORGANIZATION_SECRET_KINDS`,
  never in `ORGANIZATION_GATEWAY_KINDS`) is the one organization value that leaves the API:
  only to the run credential, from `GET /secrets/{slug}?scope=organization`, through
  `organization_subscription_for_runtime`. The runner uses it like a project login.

- Organization-scoped actions are decided only by `decide_organization`
  (`oss/src/core/access/organizations.py`). It allows a browser-session human acting as
  itself, with no run envelope, whose organization role is `owner` or `admin`. It reads
  the member row uncached and nothing else, so project RBAC shortcuts (the EE no-RBAC
  bypass, the organization-owner shortcut) never apply.
- An agent names its connection by scope and slug (`project`, the default, or
  `organization`). Nothing is inherited or overridden: a project slug reads project rows
  only, no connection means the project default, and an organization connection resolves
  only by `VaultService.get_organization_connection` (or `get_available_organization_secret_by_id`
  for a bound reference), in the gateway namespace `organization`. `SecretsResolver` is built
  per plane; only the LLM plane answers an organization connection. The `/secrets/` routes
  serve both owners. The caller states the owner (`scope`, default `project`); with
  `organization` the route runs `decide_organization`, otherwise it is the project route as
  before. `PUT /secrets/{id}/projects` addresses organization rows only. `GET /secrets/?include_organization=true` adds the organization
  rows available to the project without values (also for the `secret-resolve` grant).
- A project's vault lives in ONE cache entry (`effective_secrets`, keyed on the full
  project id), filled by one statement (`SecretsDAO.load_effective`), with the project's
  rows and the available organization rows. Do not add a second cache read for
  organization rows. Project writes invalidate it with the project-wide invalidation;
  organization writes delete each project's entry after the commit.
